record.paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
record.context_brief: curves on surfaces of general type
record.original_question: Let V be an algebraic surface with positive canonical bundle, and let f:C -> V be a holomorphic mapping. Must the image f(C) lie in an algebraic curve in V?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $V$ be a smooth complex projective algebraic surface whose canonical bundle $K_V$ is ample (so that $V$ is of general type with positive canonical class). Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to V$ be a non-constant holomorphic mapping from the complex plane into $V$. Must the image $f(\mathbb{C})$ be contained in a (proper) algebraic curve in $V$? Equivalently, must every entire holomorphic curve in such a surface $V$ be algebraically degenerate?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Green-Griffiths(-Lang) conjecture specialized to surfaces of general type. It is known to be open in general for surfaces of general type, but has been established in important cases: McQuillan proved it for projective surfaces of general type satisfying $c_1^2 > c_2$ (positive second Segre number), via the foliation/Ahlfors-Nevanlinna theory approach. Further partial results exist for surfaces with additional structure (e.g., certain foliated surfaces, Shimura surfaces, and generic high-degree hypersurfaces in higher dimensions by Diverio-Merker-Rousseau and Demailly). The general case for arbitrary surfaces of general type remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: McQuillan's approach to the Green-Griffiths conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: McQuillan proved the Green-Griffiths conjecture for a projective surface X with c_1^2(X) > c_2(X).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proved for surfaces of general type with positive second Segre number.

status_evidence.title: Recent results on the Kobayashi and Green-Griffiths-Lang conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of recent progress on the Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture, including partial results for general type varieties.
status_evidence.claim: The general Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture remains open; only partial results are known.
